question.value: What are the large-scale spatial distribution and radial abundance profiles of SiO, SiS and CS in the envelope of IRC+10216, and what do they say about its mass-loss history and photo-dissociation?

evidence.quote: Here we provide new observational constraints to the molecular emission of IRC + 10$^{\circ}$216 impinging on the nature of its mass-loss history and photo-dissociation processes
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2013.1.00432.S.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: ~84.0-115.5 GHz with five spectral setups; effective resolution 0.488 MHz (channel spacing 0.244 MHz)

evidence.quote: The total frequency coverage was achieved by using five different spectral setups with an effective spectral resolution of 0.488 MHz (channel spacing 0.244 MHz).
We used the C34-7 and C34-2 configurations (extended and compact, respectively).

baselines.value: Extended up to ~1600 m; compact 13 m to 390 m

evidence.quote: The compact configuration provided baselines as low as 13 m and up to 390 m
resulting in synthesised beam sizes as small as $\sim$0$''$6
resulting into maximum recoverable scales in the range of $\sim$23$''$ up to $\sim$32$''$ depending on the frequency
The observations were taken during several runs on December 4, 2014, and on June 29, July 4, 5, and 19, 2015.

provided.value: OTF maps 96x96 arcsec at ~80-116 GHz to recover flux filtered out by ALMA, merged with ALMA

evidence.quote: IRAM-30 m on-the-fly (OTF) observations were carried out on June 7–11, 2015, in order to recover the flux filtered out by ALMA.

what.value: Kinetic temperature profile and mass-loss rate 2.7e-5 Msun/yr

evidence.quote: The updated parameters are the kinetic temperature radial profile and the mass-loss rate, which have been recently estimated in (cite: gue18).

what.value: Collisional rate coefficients for SiO, SiS, CS with H2

evidence.quote: for SiO we used the values from (cite: day06) and (cite: bal17)

pipeline_or_manual.value: Initial calibration in CASA with ALMA-provided scripts; self-calibration in GILDAS

evidence.quote: We did an initial calibration of the ALMA data with the Common Astronomy Software Applications (cite: mcm07) by using the scripts provided by the ALMA team.

flux_calibrator.value: Ganymede or Callisto in half of tracks; archive fluxes of J0854+201, J1058+015, J0854+2006 otherwise

evidence.quote: In half of the tracks, observations of Ganymede or Callisto were performed to calibrate absolute amplitudes
we estimate an accuracy in the flux calibration better than 15%

self_calibration.value: Self-calibration on compact continuum emission with GILDAS, per track

evidence.quote: for every track the standard phase calibration was improved by self-calibrating with the very compact source continuum emission, by using the Grenoble Image and Line Data Analysis System (GILDAS) software package.
the Steer-Dewdney-Ito algorithm (cite: ste84) was used during the cleaning process

analysis_steps.goal: Merge ALMA and IRAM-30m and image cubes

method.value: UVSHORT pseudo-visibility merging, then SDI cleaning, natural and robust 0.5 weights

evidence.quote: This was done by using the UVSHORT task in the GILDAS software package that uses the pseudo-visibility technique

validation.value: Relative amplitude calibration checked in uv-plane; cleaning methods compared

evidence.quote: In all the cases a comparison was made between the different cleaning methods to ensure the consistency and quality of our results.

analysis_steps.goal: Extract azimuthal averages at systemic velocity channel and PV diagrams

method.value: Azimuthal average of brightness in the v* channel of merged cubes; moment 0, PV diagrams

evidence.quote: Azimuthal averages of the brightness distribution of the ALMA-30 m merged data of the channel corresponding to the systemic velocity of IRC + 10$^{\circ}$216 are presented

analysis_steps.goal: Radiative transfer modelling of radial abundance profiles

method.value: LVG statistical equilibrium plus ray-tracing in spherical CSE of 100 log-spaced shells; abundance profiles adjusted to reproduce azimuthal averages

evidence.quote: It is divided according to a spherical shell gridding of 100 shells evenly spaced on a logarithmic scale for the radius.

key_parameters.value: d = 123 pc; R* = 4e13 cm; T* = 2330 K; Mdot = 2.7e-5 Msun/yr; vexp 5/11/14.5 km/s; microturbulence 1 km/s; gas-to-dust 300

evidence.quote: Mass-loss rate ($\dot{M}$) | 2.7$\times$10$^{-5}$ $M_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$

assumptions.value: Spherical envelope, constant expansion velocity, collisions with H2 only

evidence.quote: The collisional rates taken into account to solve the statistical equilibrium equations consider only collisions with H$_2$.

fitting.value: Manual adjustment of abundance profiles to match azimuthal averages on average; no formal fit stated

evidence.quote: Our purpose is to derive the radial abundance profiles that reproduce the azimuthal averages observed, at least up to a level where model predictions are on average compatible with the observations.

validation.value: Synthetic spectra compared with IRAM-30m spectra; IR pumping test

evidence.quote: we tested the accuracy of the model to predict the observed spectrum of the emission lines towards IRC + 10$^{\circ}$216 as observed with the IRAM-30 m antenna

method.value: Gas-phase photo-induced chemistry network (~8000 reactions) with parent abundances updated from step 3

evidence.quote: The chemical network encompasses about 8 000 gas-phase, photo-induced, and cosmic-ray reactions

key_parameters.value: cosmic-ray ionisation rate 1.2e-17 s-1; NH/Av 1.5 times lower than classical; initial radius 2e14 cm

evidence.quote: The adopted cosmic-ray ionisation rate of H$_2$ is 1.2$\times$10$^{-17}$ s$^{-1}$ (cite: agu06).

assumptions.value: SiS photo-dissociation rate assumed equal to SiO

evidence.quote: In the case of SiS, there are no estimates of its photo-dissociation rate, thus as an educated guess, we assumed the same value than that of SiO.

validation.value: Compared fall-off radii with observations and RT results

evidence.quote: these predictions are on average below a factor of 1.5, being the fall-off distances of the chemical models larger than the observational measurements
We did an initial calibration of the ALMA data with the Common Astronomy Software Applications (cite: mcm07)
This work has made use of GILDAS[^3] and CASA[^4] softwares to reduce and analyse data.
For SiO, we derive a fractional abundance of $\sim$10$^{-7}$

results_numeric.quantity: Fractional abundance of CS in innermost CSE

evidence.quote: we derive an average fractional abundance of $\sim$10$^{-6}$ in the innermost CSE, decreasing down to $\sim$5$\times$10$^{-7}$ between $\sim$100 and 300 $R_{*}$
For SiS, we find an average abundance of $\sim$1–2$\times$10$^{-6}$ in the region up to $\sim$70–100 $R_{*}$
the first molecule to disappear from the gas phase is SiS (at $\sim$600 $R_{*}$), then SiO (at $\sim$700–800 $R_{*}$), and significantly farther, CS (at $\sim$1000 $R_{*}$)

results_numeric.quantity: Kinematical age of shell at ~420 R*

evidence.quote: the kinematical age for a shell located at $\sim$420 $R_{*}$ would be $\sim$365 years

findings_qualitative.value: Emission shows arcs and shells; SiS J=5-4 shows horn emission suggested to be maser from IR line overlap

evidence.quote: The most plausible explanation for this scenario is maser emission of the $J$=5–4 line, probably as a consequence of an IR line overlap as we discuss below.

claims.hypothesis: Is the mass loss of IRC+10216 episodic?
claims.experiment: Mapped SiO, SiS, CS at 3 mm, computed azimuthal averages, compared with dust shells
claims.result: Common shells at ~150, 315, 420, 560 R* in all lines coincident with dust shells
claims.finding: Over-dense shells point to variable mass loss on timescales of hundreds of years

evidence.quote: pose strong evidences of a variable mass-loss process acting on IRC + 10$^{\circ}$216 with timescales of hundreds of years

claims.hypothesis: Can a standard gas-phase chemical model reproduce the observed sizes?
claims.experiment: Chemical model with RT-derived parent abundances
claims.result: Right sequence of dissociation radii, but fall-off ~1.5 times farther than observed; no shells
claims.finding: Model qualitatively consistent but too simple

evidence.quote: the chemical model predicts fall-off distances $\sim$1.5 times larger than those derived from the observations and radiative transfer analysis

why_this_method.value: Single-dish data needed for large-scale flux missed by interferometer

evidence.quote: Large-scale flux is provided by short-space observations, thus, single-dish observations must be considered if the aim is to study the complete molecular emission of an extended object.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Hogbom CLEAN rejected as it can introduce artificial clumpiness in extended emission

evidence.quote: given that (cite: hog74) can introduce artificial clumpiness when generating images of objects that have extended emission

limitations_admitted.value: Model based on single line for SiO and CS, two for SiS; degeneracy between density and abundance

evidence.quote: our study is based solely on the analysis of just a single line in the cases of SiO and CS, and two lines in the case of SiS
